issue: wósn̥-kʷe-ge h₁áyoh₂er: 'and I too will take' has no 1sg pronoun (h₁eǵ-ge); -ge emphasizes the object, so the 'too' is lost. ph₃ént is 3pl although the same two men took 3du gʷm̥tā́m before (62fdfd4e has ph₃tā́m in the same situation). kʷyéh₁tis is 'rest, quiet' (the lexicon says 'not a treaty'), so it is stretched for the peace that settles a blood-price.
gʷm̥yóh₂ is 1sg thematic present ('I come'); 'the wolf comes' needs 3sg gʷm̥yéti.

HréwdH- means 'weep, wail, bellow', not 'call'; h₁íns HrudHtóm 'cry out to them' (acc. of addressee) and 'this one cried out' to summon cattle stretch the sense. Morphology fine (h₁stā́m, widḗr, gʷh₂ént, ḱluwént).
somHéh₂ 'lone': *somHós is primarily 'same, alike' (Gk homós, Goth sama), so 'alone' is weakly supported; *óynos would be safer. Rest fine (skinédti, dat. possessor + 3du h₁stés).
h₁ésyeh₂s pótnih₂ h₁ésmi: h₁ésmi is 1sg ('I am'); 'You are its mistress' needs 2sg h₁ési.
h₁ím stéygʰes ph₂sdʰí: in the engine's paradigm stéygʰes is the nom. pl. ('paths'); 'on the path' needs loc. stéygʰi (as in b8674ce8) or gen. stigʰés.
kn̥h₂ónks used as the object of bʰéret: the -s is a nom. sg. ending (stem *kn̥h₂onk-), so acc. should be *kn̥h₂ónkm̥. The engine paradigm wrongly keeps -s in the stem (gen. kn̥h₂ónksos).

The same two sons are addressed in 2pl (ǵeǵn̥h₁é perf. 2pl, wos) and then 2du (stundtóm); tóh₁ (nom./acc. du.) used for 'to them' where a dative is expected (dual obliques go to the plural: tóybʰos); próti alone drops 'one another'.
méh₂ter toy gʷíh₃weti?: méh₂ter is the vocative; the subject needs nom. méh₂tēr (used correctly later in the same text).
dyéw ph₂térm̥: ph₂térm̥ is acc.; the address 'Father Sky' needs voc. ph₂ter (as in fa326bd3 dyéw ph₂ter); case disagreement with voc. dyéw.

Scholarly 'King and God' variant, mixed conventions: tom unaccented, wewked with -d and no accent (handbook *wéwket). Accusative addressee tom h₃rḗǵm̥ is defensible (Vedic vac-/brū- + acc.), though dative tósmey h₃r̥ǵéy would be more usual.

widn̥tbʰ(y)os is dat. PL ('to us seeing', left over from Schleicher's horses' speech) but agrees with sg. moi ('my heart pains me'); needs dat. sg. *widn̥téy. Parenthesized (y) is notation, not text; tu ('then') is untranslated.

Kortlandt-style scholarly version: grammatically consistent (widntéy agrees with moy), but uses notation for optional segments ((h₁)éḱwobʰos, ewewkʷe(t)) and leaves syllabic resonants unmarked (widntéy, dʰǵʰmónm, h₂éǵontm for -n̥-/-m̥); ḱḗrd/-toy are school-specific.
